column4: If your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you. For it is more profitable for you that one of your members should perish, than for your whole body to be cast into Gehenna.
column5: And if thy right eye offend thee, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that thy whole body should be cast into hell.

column4: If your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off, and throw it away from you. For it is more profitable for you that one of your members should perish, than for your whole body to be cast into Gehenna.
column5: And if thy right hand offend thee, cut it off, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that thy whole body should be cast into hell.

column4: “It was also said, ‘Whoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorce,’
column5: It hath been said, Whosoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorcement:

column4: but I tell you that whoever puts away his wife, except for the cause of sexual immorality, makes her an adulteress; and whoever marries her when she is put away commits adultery.
column5: But I say unto you, That whosoever shall put away his wife, saving for the cause of fornication, causeth her to commit adultery: and whosoever shall marry her that is divorced committeth adultery.

column4: “Again you have heard that it was said to the ancient ones, ‘You shall not make false vows, but shall perform to the Lord your vows,’
column5: Again, ye have heard that it hath been said by them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto the Lord thine oaths:

column4: but I tell you, don’t swear at all: neither by heaven, for it is the throne of God;
column5: But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God’s throne:

column4: nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet; nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
column5: Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King.

column4: Neither shall you swear by your head, for you can’t make one hair white or black.
column5: Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black.

column4: But let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes’ and your ‘No’ be ‘No.’ Whatever is more than these is of the evil one.
column5: But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.

column4: “You have heard that it was said, ‘An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.’
column5: Ye have heard that it hath been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth:

column4: But I tell you, don’t resist him who is evil; but whoever strikes you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also.
column5: But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil: but whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.

column4: If anyone sues you to take away your coat, let him have your cloak also.
column5: And if any man will sue thee at the law, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloke also.

column4: Whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two.
column5: And whosoever shall compel thee to go a mile, go with him twain.

column4: Give to him who asks you, and don’t turn away him who desires to borrow from you.
column5: Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away.

column4: “You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’
column5: Ye have heard that it hath been said, Thou shalt love thy neighbour, and hate thine enemy.

column4: But I tell you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat you and persecute you,
column5: But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;

column4: that you may be children of your Father who is in heaven. For he makes his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the just and the unjust.
column5: That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.

column4: For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Don’t even the tax collectors do the same?
column5: For if ye love them which love you, what reward have ye? do not even the publicans the same?

column4: If you only greet your friends, what more do you do than others? Don’t even the tax collectors do the same?
column5: And if ye salute your brethren only, what do ye more than others ? do not even the publicans so?

column4: Therefore you shall be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect.
column5: Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.

column4: “Be careful that you don’t do your charitable giving before men, to be seen by them, or else you have no reward from your Father who is in heaven.
column5: Take heed that ye do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise ye have no reward of your Father which is in heaven.

column4: Therefore when you do merciful deeds, don’t sound a trumpet before yourself, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may get glory from men. Most certainly I tell you, they have received their reward.
column5: Therefore when thou doest thine alms, do not sound a trumpet before thee, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may have glory of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.

column4: But when you do merciful deeds, don’t let your left hand know what your right hand does,
column5: But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth:

column4: so that your merciful deeds may be in secret, then your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.
column5: That thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward thee openly.

column4: “When you pray, you shall not be as the hypocrites, for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen by men. Most certainly, I tell you, they have received their reward.
column5: And when thou prayest, thou shalt not be as the hypocrites are : for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.

column4: But you, when you pray, enter into your inner room, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret, and your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.
column5: But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret; and thy Father which seeth in secret shall reward thee openly.

column4: In praying, don’t use vain repetitions, as the Gentiles do; for they think that they will be heard for their much speaking.
column5: But when ye pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do : for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.

column4: Therefore don’t be like them, for your Father knows what things you need, before you ask him.
column5: Be not ye therefore like unto them: for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him.

column4: Pray like this: ‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.
column5: After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.

column4: Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.
column5: Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.

column4: Give us today our daily bread.
column5: Give us this day our daily bread.

column4: Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.
column5: And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.

column4: Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory forever. Amen.’
column5: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.

column4: “For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
column5: For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:

column4: But if you don’t forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
column5: But if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.

column4: “Moreover when you fast, don’t be like the hypocrites, with sad faces. For they disfigure their faces, that they may be seen by men to be fasting. Most certainly I tell you, they have received their reward.
column5: Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.

column4: But you, when you fast, anoint your head, and wash your face;
column5: But thou, when thou fastest, anoint thine head, and wash thy face;

column4: so that you are not seen by men to be fasting, but by your Father who is in secret, and your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you.
column5: That thou appear not unto men to fast, but unto thy Father which is in secret: and thy Father, which seeth in secret, shall reward thee openly.

column4: “Don’t lay up treasures for yourselves on the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal;
column5: Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal:

column4: but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consume, and where thieves don’t break through and steal;
column5: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal:

column4: for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
column5: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

column4: “The lamp of the body is the eye. If therefore your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light.
column5: The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.

column4: But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in you is darkness, how great is the darkness!
column5: But if thine eye be evil, thy whole body shall be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great is that darkness!

column4: “No one can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other; or else he will be devoted to one and despise the other. You can’t serve both God and Mammon.
column5: No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.

column4: Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life: what you will eat, or what you will drink; nor yet for your body, what you will wear. Isn’t life more than food, and the body more than clothing?
column5: Therefore I say unto you, Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on. Is not the life more than meat, and the body than raiment?

column4: See the birds of the sky, that they don’t sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren’t you of much more value than they?
column5: Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?

column4: “Which of you, by being anxious, can add one moment to his lifespan?
column5: Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit unto his stature?

column4: Why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow. They don’t toil, neither do they spin,
column5: And why take ye thought for raiment? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin:

column4: yet I tell you that even Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one of these.
column5: And yet I say unto you, That even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.

column4: But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which today exists, and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, won’t he much more clothe you, you of little faith?
column5: Wherefore, if God so clothe the grass of the field, which to day is, and to morrow is cast into the oven, shall he not much more clothe you, O ye of little faith?

column4: “Therefore don’t be anxious, saying, ‘What will we eat?’, ‘What will we drink?’ or, ‘With what will we be clothed?’
column5: Therefore take no thought, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed?

column4: For the Gentiles seek after all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.
column5: (For after all these things do the Gentiles seek:) for your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things.

column4: But seek first God’s Kingdom, and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.
column5: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.

column4: Therefore don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day’s own evil is sufficient.
column5: Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.

column4: “Don’t judge, so that you won’t be judged.
column5: Judge not, that ye be not judged.

column4: For with whatever judgment you judge, you will be judged; and with whatever measure you measure, it will be measured to you.
column5: For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged: and with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you again.

column4: Why do you see the speck that is in your brother’s eye, but don’t consider the beam that is in your own eye?
column5: And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother’s eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye?

column4: Or how will you tell your brother, ‘Let me remove the speck from your eye;’ and behold, the beam is in your own eye?
column5: Or how wilt thou say to thy brother, Let me pull out the mote out of thine eye; and, behold, a beam is in thine own eye?

column4: You hypocrite! First remove the beam out of your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck out of your brother’s eye.
column5: Thou hypocrite, first cast out the beam out of thine own eye; and then shalt thou see clearly to cast out the mote out of thy brother’s eye.

column4: “Don’t give that which is holy to the dogs, neither throw your pearls before the pigs, lest perhaps they trample them under their feet, and turn and tear you to pieces.
column5: Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you.

column4: “Ask, and it will be given you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened for you.
column5: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you:

column4: For everyone who asks receives. He who seeks finds. To him who knocks it will be opened.
column5: For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.

column4: Or who is there among you, who, if his son asks him for bread, will give him a stone?
column5: Or what man is there of you, whom if his son ask bread, will he give him a stone?

column4: Or if he asks for a fish, who will give him a serpent?
column5: Or if he ask a fish, will he give him a serpent?

column4: If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who is in heaven give good things to those who ask him!
column5: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?

column4: Therefore whatever you desire for men to do to you, you shall also do to them; for this is the law and the prophets.
column5: Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.

column4: “Enter in by the narrow gate; for wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many are those who enter in by it.
column5: Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat:

column4: How narrow is the gate, and restricted is the way that leads to life! Few are those who find it.
column5: Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.

column4: “Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly are ravening wolves.
column5: Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves.

column4: By their fruits you will know them. Do you gather grapes from thorns, or figs from thistles?
column5: Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?

column4: Even so, every good tree produces good fruit; but the corrupt tree produces evil fruit.
column5: Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit.

column4: A good tree can’t produce evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree produce good fruit.
column5: A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.

column4: Every tree that doesn’t grow good fruit is cut down, and thrown into the fire.
column5: Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.

column4: Therefore by their fruits you will know them.
column5: Wherefore by their fruits ye shall know them.

column4: Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven; but he who does the will of my Father who is in heaven.
column5: Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.

column4: Many will tell me in that day, ‘Lord, Lord, didn’t we prophesy in your name, in your name cast out demons, and in your name do many mighty works?’
column5: Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works?

column4: Then I will tell them, ‘I never knew you. Depart from me, you who work iniquity.’
column5: And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.

column4: “Everyone therefore who hears these words of mine, and does them, I will liken him to a wise man, who built his house on a rock.
column5: Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock:

column4: The rain came down, the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat on that house; and it didn’t fall, for it was founded on the rock.
column5: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.

column4: Everyone who hears these words of mine, and doesn’t do them will be like a foolish man, who built his house on the sand.
column5: And every one that heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, which built his house upon the sand:

column4: The rain came down, the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat on that house; and it fell—and great was its fall.”
column5: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell: and great was the fall of it.

column4: When Jesus had finished saying these things, the multitudes were astonished at his teaching,
column5: And it came to pass, when Jesus had ended these sayings, the people were astonished at his doctrine:

column4: for he taught them with authority, and not like the scribes.
column5: For he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.

column4: When he came down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him.
column5: When he was come down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him.

column4: Behold, a leper came to him and worshiped him, saying, “Lord, if you want to, you can make me clean.”
column5: And, behold, there came a leper and worshipped him, saying, Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.

column4: Jesus stretched out his hand, and touched him, saying, “I want to. Be made clean.” Immediately his leprosy was cleansed.
column5: And Jesus put forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will; be thou clean. And immediately his leprosy was cleansed.

column4: Jesus said to him, “See that you tell nobody, but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”
column5: And Jesus saith unto him, See thou tell no man; but go thy way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.

column4: When he came into Capernaum, a centurion came to him, asking him,
column5: And when Jesus was entered into Capernaum, there came unto him a centurion, beseeching him,

column4: and saying, “Lord, my servant lies in the house paralyzed, grievously tormented.”
column5: And saying, Lord, my servant lieth at home sick of the palsy, grievously tormented.

column4: Jesus said to him, “I will come and heal him.”
column5: And Jesus saith unto him, I will come and heal him.

column4: The centurion answered, “Lord, I’m not worthy for you to come under my roof. Just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
column5: The centurion answered and said, Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof: but speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed.

column4: For I am also a man under authority, having under myself soldiers. I tell this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; and tell another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and tell my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”
column5: For I am a man under authority, having soldiers under me: and I say to this man , Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it .

column4: When Jesus heard it, he marveled, and said to those who followed, “Most certainly I tell you, I haven’t found so great a faith, not even in Israel.
column5: When Jesus heard it , he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.

column4: I tell you that many will come from the east and the west, and will sit down with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the Kingdom of Heaven,
column5: And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.

column4: but the children of the Kingdom will be thrown out into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”
column5: But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

column4: Jesus said to the centurion, “Go your way. Let it be done for you as you have believed.” His servant was healed in that hour.
column5: And Jesus said unto the centurion, Go thy way; and as thou hast believed, so be it done unto thee. And his servant was healed in the selfsame hour.

column4: When Jesus came into Peter’s house, he saw his wife’s mother lying sick with a fever.
column5: And when Jesus was come into Peter’s house, he saw his wife’s mother laid, and sick of a fever.

column4: He touched her hand, and the fever left her. She got up and served him.
column5: And he touched her hand, and the fever left her: and she arose, and ministered unto them.

column4: When evening came, they brought to him many possessed with demons. He cast out the spirits with a word, and healed all who were sick;
column5: When the even was come, they brought unto him many that were possessed with devils: and he cast out the spirits with his word, and healed all that were sick:

column4: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying, “He took our infirmities, and bore our diseases.”
column5: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying, Himself took our infirmities, and bare our sicknesses.

column4: Now when Jesus saw great multitudes around him, he gave the order to depart to the other side.
column5: Now when Jesus saw great multitudes about him, he gave commandment to depart unto the other side.

column4: A scribe came, and said to him, “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.”
column5: And a certain scribe came, and said unto him, Master, I will follow thee whithersoever thou goest.

column4: Jesus said to him, “The foxes have holes, and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”
column5: And Jesus saith unto him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air have nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head.

column4: Another of his disciples said to him, “Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father.”
column5: And another of his disciples said unto him, Lord, suffer me first to go and bury my father.

column4: But Jesus said to him, “Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead.”
column5: But Jesus said unto him, Follow me; and let the dead bury their dead.

column4: When he got into a boat, his disciples followed him.
column5: And when he was entered into a ship, his disciples followed him.

column4: Behold, a violent storm came up on the sea, so much that the boat was covered with the waves, but he was asleep.
column5: And, behold, there arose a great tempest in the sea, insomuch that the ship was covered with the waves: but he was asleep.

column4: They came to him, and woke him up, saying, “Save us, Lord! We are dying!”
column5: And his disciples came to him , and awoke him, saying, Lord, save us: we perish.

column4: He said to them, “Why are you fearful, O you of little faith?” Then he got up, rebuked the wind and the sea, and there was a great calm.
column5: And he saith unto them, Why are ye fearful, O ye of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.

column4: The men marveled, saying, “What kind of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”
column5: But the men marvelled, saying, What manner of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him!

column4: When he came to the other side, into the country of the Gergesenes, two people possessed by demons met him there, coming out of the tombs, exceedingly fierce, so that nobody could pass that way.
column5: And when he was come to the other side into the country of the Gergesenes, there met him two possessed with devils, coming out of the tombs, exceeding fierce, so that no man might pass by that way.

column4: Behold, they cried out, saying, “What do we have to do with you, Jesus, Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the time?”
column5: And, behold, they cried out, saying, What have we to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of God? art thou come hither to torment us before the time?

column4: Now there was a herd of many pigs feeding far away from them.
column5: And there was a good way off from them an herd of many swine feeding.

column4: The demons begged him, saying, “If you cast us out, permit us to go away into the herd of pigs.”
column5: So the devils besought him, saying, If thou cast us out, suffer us to go away into the herd of swine.

column4: He said to them, “Go!” They came out, and went into the herd of pigs: and behold, the whole herd of pigs rushed down the cliff into the sea, and died in the water.
column5: And he said unto them, Go. And when they were come out, they went into the herd of swine: and, behold, the whole herd of swine ran violently down a steep place into the sea, and perished in the waters.

column4: Those who fed them fled, and went away into the city, and told everything, including what happened to those who were possessed with demons.
column5: And they that kept them fled, and went their ways into the city, and told every thing, and what was befallen to the possessed of the devils.

column4: Behold, all the city came out to meet Jesus. When they saw him, they begged that he would depart from their borders.
column5: And, behold, the whole city came out to meet Jesus: and when they saw him, they besought him that he would depart out of their coasts.

column4: He entered into a boat, and crossed over, and came into his own city.
column5: And he entered into a ship, and passed over, and came into his own city.

column4: Behold, they brought to him a man who was paralyzed, lying on a bed. Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic, “Son, cheer up! Your sins are forgiven you.”
column5: And, behold, they brought to him a man sick of the palsy, lying on a bed: and Jesus seeing their faith said unto the sick of the palsy; Son, be of good cheer; thy sins be forgiven thee.

column4: Behold, some of the scribes said to themselves, “This man blasphemes.”
column5: And, behold, certain of the scribes said within themselves, This man blasphemeth.

column4: Jesus, knowing their thoughts, said, “Why do you think evil in your hearts?
column5: And Jesus knowing their thoughts said, Wherefore think ye evil in your hearts?

column4: For which is easier, to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven;’ or to say, ‘Get up, and walk?’
column5: For whether is easier, to say, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and walk?

column4: But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins-” (then he said to the paralytic), “Get up, and take up your mat, and go to your house.”

column4: Then one possessed by a demon, blind and mute, was brought to him and he healed him, so that the blind and mute man both spoke and saw.

column5: But when the Pharisees heard it , they said, This fellow doth not cast out devils, but by Beelzebub the prince of the devils.

column5: And Jesus knew their thoughts, and said unto them, Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation; and every city or house divided against itself shall not stand:

column4: If Satan casts out Satan, he is divided against himself. How then will his kingdom stand?
column5: And if Satan cast out Satan, he is divided against himself; how shall then his kingdom stand?

column4: If I by Beelzebul cast out demons, by whom do your children cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.
column5: And if I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your children cast them out? therefore they shall be your judges.

column4: But if I by the Spirit of God cast out demons, then God’s Kingdom has come upon you.
column5: But if I cast out devils by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God is come unto you.

column4: Or how can one enter into the house of the strong man, and plunder his goods, unless he first bind the strong man? Then he will plunder his house.

column4: “He who is not with me is against me, and he who doesn’t gather with me, scatters.

column5: Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven unto men.

column5: And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.

column4: “Either make the tree good, and its fruit good, or make the tree corrupt, and its fruit corrupt; for the tree is known by its fruit.
column5: Either make the tree good, and his fruit good; or else make the tree corrupt, and his fruit corrupt: for the tree is known by his fruit.

column5: O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.

column5: A good man out of the good treasure of the heart bringeth forth good things: and an evil man out of the evil treasure bringeth forth evil things.

column4: I tell you that every idle word that men speak, they will give account of it in the day of judgment.

column4: For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.”
column5: For by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned.

column5: Then certain of the scribes and of the Pharisees answered, saying, Master, we would see a sign from thee.

column4: But he answered them, “An evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign, but no sign will be given to it but the sign of Jonah the prophet.
column5: But he answered and said unto them, An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas:

column5: For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale’s belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

column5: The men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: because they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here.

column5: The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for she came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here.

column5: Then he saith, I will return into my house from whence I came out; and when he is come, he findeth it empty, swept, and garnished.

column5: Then goeth he, and taketh with himself seven other spirits more wicked than himself, and they enter in and dwell there: and the last state of that man is worse than the first. Even so shall it be also unto this wicked generation.

column4: While he was yet speaking to the multitudes, behold, his mother and his brothers stood outside, seeking to speak to him.
column5: While he yet talked to the people, behold, his mother and his brethren stood without, desiring to speak with him.

column5: Then one said unto him, Behold, thy mother and thy brethren stand without, desiring to speak with thee.

column5: But he answered and said unto him that told him, Who is my mother? and who are my brethren?

column5: And he stretched forth his hand toward his disciples, and said, Behold my mother and my brethren!

column5: For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.

column5: And great multitudes were gathered together unto him, so that he went into a ship, and sat; and the whole multitude stood on the shore.

column5: And when the sun was up, they were scorched; and because they had no root, they withered away.

column5: And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprung up, and choked them:

column5: But other fell into good ground, and brought forth fruit, some an hundredfold, some sixtyfold, some thirtyfold.

column4: He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”
column5: Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.

column5: And the disciples came, and said unto him, Why speakest thou unto them in parables?

column5: He answered and said unto them, Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.

column4: For whoever has, to him will be given, and he will have abundance, but whoever doesn’t have, from him will be taken away even that which he has.
column5: For whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance: but whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that he hath.

column4: Therefore I speak to them in parables, because seeing they don’t see, and hearing, they don’t hear, neither do they understand.
column5: Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand.

column4: In them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled, which says, ‘By hearing you will hear, and will in no way understand; Seeing you will see, and will in no way perceive:
column5: And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive:

column4: for this people’s heart has grown callous, their ears are dull of hearing, they have closed their eyes; or else perhaps they might perceive with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and would turn again; and I would heal them.’
column5: For this people’s heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.

column4: “But blessed are your eyes, for they see; and your ears, for they hear.
column5: But blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear.

column4: For most certainly I tell you that many prophets and righteous men desired to see the things which you see, and didn’t see them; and to hear the things which you hear, and didn’t hear them.
column5: For verily I say unto you, That many prophets and righteous men have desired to see those things which ye see, and have not seen them ; and to hear those things which ye hear, and have not heard them.

column4: “Hear, then, the parable of the farmer.
column5: Hear ye therefore the parable of the sower.

column4: When anyone hears the word of the Kingdom, and doesn’t understand it, the evil one comes, and snatches away that which has been sown in his heart. This is what was sown by the roadside.
column5: When any one heareth the word of the kingdom, and understandeth it not, then cometh the wicked one , and catcheth away that which was sown in his heart. This is he which received seed by the way side.

column4: What was sown on the rocky places, this is he who hears the word, and immediately with joy receives it;
column5: But he that received the seed into stony places, the same is he that heareth the word, and anon with joy receiveth it;

column4: yet he has no root in himself, but endures for a while. When oppression or persecution arises because of the word, immediately he stumbles.
column5: Yet hath he not root in himself, but dureth for a while: for when tribulation or persecution ariseth because of the word, by and by he is offended.

column4: What was sown among the thorns, this is he who hears the word, but the cares of this age and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word, and he becomes unfruitful.
column5: He also that received seed among the thorns is he that heareth the word; and the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, and he becometh unfruitful.

column4: What was sown on the good ground, this is he who hears the word, and understands it, who most certainly bears fruit, and produces, some one hundred times as much, some sixty, and some thirty.”
column5: But he that received seed into the good ground is he that heareth the word, and understandeth it ; which also beareth fruit, and bringeth forth, some an hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.

column4: He set another parable before them, saying, “The Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field,
column5: Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field:

column4: but while people slept, his enemy came and sowed darnel weeds also among the wheat, and went away.
column5: But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went his way.

column4: But when the blade sprang up and produced fruit, then the darnel weeds appeared also.
column5: But when the blade was sprung up, and brought forth fruit, then appeared the tares also.

column4: The servants of the householder came and said to him, ‘Sir, didn’t you sow good seed in your field? Where did these darnel weeds come from?’
column5: So the servants of the householder came and said unto him, Sir, didst not thou sow good seed in thy field? from whence then hath it tares?

column4: “He said to them, ‘An enemy has done this.’ “The servants asked him, ‘Do you want us to go and gather them up?’
column5: He said unto them, An enemy hath done this. The servants said unto him, Wilt thou then that we go and gather them up?

column4: “But he said, ‘No, lest perhaps while you gather up the darnel weeds, you root up the wheat with them.
column5: But he said, Nay; lest while ye gather up the tares, ye root up also the wheat with them.

column4: Let both grow together until the harvest, and in the harvest time I will tell the reapers, “First, gather up the darnel weeds, and bind them in bundles to burn them; but gather the wheat into my barn.” ’ ”
column5: Let both grow together until the harvest: and in the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, Gather ye together first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them: but gather the wheat into my barn.

column4: He set another parable before them, saying, “The Kingdom of Heaven is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field;
column5: Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field:

column4: which indeed is smaller than all seeds. But when it is grown, it is greater than the herbs, and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in its branches.”
column5: Which indeed is the least of all seeds: but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs, and becometh a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in the branches thereof.

column4: He spoke another parable to them. “The Kingdom of Heaven is like yeast, which a woman took, and hid in three measures of meal, until it was all leavened.”
column5: Another parable spake he unto them; The kingdom of heaven is like unto leaven, which a woman took, and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened.

column4: Jesus spoke all these things in parables to the multitudes; and without a parable, he didn’t speak to them,
column5: All these things spake Jesus unto the multitude in parables; and without a parable spake he not unto them:

column4: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophet, saying, “I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the foundation of the world.”
column5: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world.

column4: Then Jesus sent the multitudes away, and went into the house. His disciples came to him, saying, “Explain to us the parable of the darnel weeds of the field.”
column5: Then Jesus sent the multitude away, and went into the house: and his disciples came unto him, saying, Declare unto us the parable of the tares of the field.

column4: He answered them, “He who sows the good seed is the Son of Man,
column5: He answered and said unto them, He that soweth the good seed is the Son of man;

column4: the field is the world; and the good seed, these are the children of the Kingdom; and the darnel weeds are the children of the evil one.
column5: The field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom; but the tares are the children of the wicked one ;

column4: The enemy who sowed them is the devil. The harvest is the end of the age, and the reapers are angels.
column5: The enemy that sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are the angels.

column4: As therefore the darnel weeds are gathered up and burned with fire; so will it be at the end of this age.
column5: As therefore the tares are gathered and burned in the fire; so shall it be in the end of this world.

column4: The Son of Man will send out his angels, and they will gather out of his Kingdom all things that cause stumbling, and those who do iniquity,
column5: The Son of man shall send forth his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all things that offend, and them which do iniquity;

column4: and will cast them into the furnace of fire. There will be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.
column5: And shall cast them into a furnace of fire: there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth.

column4: Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the Kingdom of their Father. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.
column5: Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.

column4: “Again, the Kingdom of Heaven is like treasure hidden in the field, which a man found, and hid. In his joy, he goes and sells all that he has, and buys that field.
column5: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field; the which when a man hath found, he hideth, and for joy thereof goeth and selleth all that he hath, and buyeth that field.

column4: “Again, the Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who is a merchant seeking fine pearls,
column5: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a merchant man, seeking goodly pearls:

column4: who having found one pearl of great price, he went and sold all that he had, and bought it.
column5: Who, when he had found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had, and bought it.

column4: “Again, the Kingdom of Heaven is like a dragnet, that was cast into the sea, and gathered some fish of every kind,
column5: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a net, that was cast into the sea, and gathered of every kind:

column4: which, when it was filled, they drew up on the beach. They sat down, and gathered the good into containers, but the bad they threw away.
column5: Which, when it was full, they drew to shore, and sat down, and gathered the good into vessels, but cast the bad away.

column4: So will it be in the end of the world. The angels will come and separate the wicked from among the righteous,
column5: So shall it be at the end of the world: the angels shall come forth, and sever the wicked from among the just,

column4: and will cast them into the furnace of fire. There will be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.”
column5: And shall cast them into the furnace of fire: there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth.

column4: Jesus said to them, “Have you understood all these things?” They answered him, “Yes, Lord.”
column5: Jesus saith unto them, Have ye understood all these things? They say unto him, Yea, Lord.

column4: He said to them, “Therefore every scribe who has been made a disciple in the Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who is a householder, who brings out of his treasure new and old things.”
column5: Then said he unto them, Therefore every scribe which is instructed unto the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which bringeth forth out of his treasure things new and old.

column4: When Jesus had finished these parables, he departed from there.
column5: And it came to pass, that when Jesus had finished these parables, he departed thence.

column4: Coming into his own country, he taught them in their synagogue, so that they were astonished, and said, “Where did this man get this wisdom, and these mighty works?
column5: And when he was come into his own country, he taught them in their synagogue, insomuch that they were astonished, and said, Whence hath this man this wisdom, and these mighty works?

column4: Isn’t this the carpenter’s son? Isn’t his mother called Mary, and his brothers, James, Joses, Simon, and Judas?
column5: Is not this the carpenter’s son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas?

column4: Aren’t all of his sisters with us? Where then did this man get all of these things?”
column5: And his sisters, are they not all with us? Whence then hath this man all these things?

column4: They were offended by him. But Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor, except in his own country, and in his own house.”
column5: And they were offended in him. But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country, and in his own house.

column4: He didn’t do many mighty works there because of their unbelief.

column5: At that time Herod the tetrarch heard of the fame of Jesus,

column4: and said to his servants, “This is John the Baptizer. He is risen from the dead. That is why these powers work in him.”
column5: And said unto his servants, This is John the Baptist; he is risen from the dead; and therefore mighty works do shew forth themselves in him.

column5: For Herod had laid hold on John, and bound him, and put him in prison for Herodias’ sake, his brother Philip’s wife.

column4: For John said to him, “It is not lawful for you to have her.”
column5: For John said unto him, It is not lawful for thee to have her.

column5: And when he would have put him to death, he feared the multitude, because they counted him as a prophet.

column5: But when Herod’s birthday was kept, the daughter of Herodias danced before them, and pleased Herod.

column4: Whereupon he promised with an oath to give her whatever she should ask.
column5: Whereupon he promised with an oath to give her whatsoever she would ask.

column5: And she, being before instructed of her mother, said, Give me here John Baptist’s head in a charger.

column4: The king was grieved, but for the sake of his oaths, and of those who sat at the table with him, he commanded it to be given,

column4: and he sent and beheaded John in the prison.
column5: And he sent, and beheaded John in the prison.

column4: His head was brought on a platter, and given to the young lady; and she brought it to her mother.
column5: And his head was brought in a charger, and given to the damsel: and she brought it to her mother.

column4: His disciples came, and took the body, and buried it. Then they went and told Jesus.
column5: And his disciples came, and took up the body, and buried it, and went and told Jesus.

column4: Now when Jesus heard this, he withdrew from there in a boat, to a deserted place apart. When the multitudes heard it, they followed him on foot from the cities.

column5: But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me.

column5: And he cast down the pieces of silver in the temple, and departed, and went and hanged himself.

column5: Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremy the prophet, saying, And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of him that was valued, whom they of the children of Israel did value;

column4: Now Jesus stood before the governor: and the governor asked him, saying, “Are you the King of the Jews?” Jesus said to him, “So you say.”
column5: And Jesus stood before the governor: and the governor asked him, saying, Art thou the King of the Jews? And Jesus said unto him, Thou sayest.

column5: And when he was accused of the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing.

column4: Then Pilate said to him, “Don’t you hear how many things they testify against you?”
column5: Then said Pilate unto him, Hearest thou not how many things they witness against thee?

column4: He gave him no answer, not even one word, so that the governor marveled greatly.
column5: And he answered him to never a word; insomuch that the governor marvelled greatly.

column4: Now at the feast the governor was accustomed to release to the multitude one prisoner, whom they desired.
column5: Now at that feast the governor was wont to release unto the people a prisoner, whom they would.

column4: They had then a notable prisoner, called Barabbas.
column5: And they had then a notable prisoner, called Barabbas.

column4: When therefore they were gathered together, Pilate said to them, “Whom do you want me to release to you? Barabbas, or Jesus, who is called Christ?”
column5: Therefore when they were gathered together, Pilate said unto them, Whom will ye that I release unto you? Barabbas, or Jesus which is called Christ?

column4: For he knew that because of envy they had delivered him up.
column5: For he knew that for envy they had delivered him.

column5: When he was set down on the judgment seat, his wife sent unto him, saying, Have thou nothing to do with that just man: for I have suffered many things this day in a dream because of him.

column4: Now the chief priests and the elders persuaded the multitudes to ask for Barabbas, and destroy Jesus.
column5: But the chief priests and elders persuaded the multitude that they should ask Barabbas, and destroy Jesus.

column4: But the governor answered them, “Which of the two do you want me to release to you?” They said, “Barabbas!”
column5: The governor answered and said unto them, Whether of the twain will ye that I release unto you? They said, Barabbas.

column4: Pilate said to them, “What then shall I do to Jesus, who is called Christ?” They all said to him, “Let him be crucified!”
column5: Pilate saith unto them, What shall I do then with Jesus which is called Christ? They all say unto him, Let him be crucified.

column4: But the governor said, “Why? What evil has he done?” But they cried out exceedingly, saying, “Let him be crucified!”
column5: And the governor said, Why, what evil hath he done? But they cried out the more, saying, Let him be crucified.

column4: So when Pilate saw that nothing was being gained, but rather that a disturbance was starting, he took water, and washed his hands before the multitude, saying, “I am innocent of the blood of this righteous person. You see to it.”
column5: When Pilate saw that he could prevail nothing, but that rather a tumult was made, he took water, and washed his hands before the multitude, saying, I am innocent of the blood of this just person: see ye to it .

column4: All the people answered, “May his blood be on us, and on our children!”
column5: Then answered all the people, and said, His blood be on us, and on our children.

column4: Then he released to them Barabbas, but Jesus he flogged and delivered to be crucified.
column5: Then released he Barabbas unto them: and when he had scourged Jesus, he delivered him to be crucified.

column4: Then the governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the Praetorium, and gathered the whole garrison together against him.
column5: Then the soldiers of the governor took Jesus into the common hall, and gathered unto him the whole band of soldiers .

column4: They stripped him, and put a scarlet robe on him.
column5: And they stripped him, and put on him a scarlet robe.

column5: And when they had platted a crown of thorns, they put it upon his head, and a reed in his right hand: and they bowed the knee before him, and mocked him, saying, Hail, King of the Jews!

column4: They spat on him, and took the reed and struck him on the head.
column5: And they spit upon him, and took the reed, and smote him on the head.

column4: When they had mocked him, they took the robe off him, and put his clothes on him, and led him away to crucify him.
column5: And after that they had mocked him, they took the robe off from him, and put his own raiment on him, and led him away to crucify him .

column4: As they came out, they found a man of Cyrene, Simon by name, and they compelled him to go with them, that he might carry his cross.
column5: And as they came out, they found a man of Cyrene, Simon by name: him they compelled to bear his cross.

column4: When they came to a place called “Golgotha”, that is to say, “The place of a skull,”
column5: And when they were come unto a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull,

column4: they gave him sour wine to drink mixed with gall. When he had tasted it, he would not drink.

column4: When they had crucified him, they divided his clothing among them, casting lots,

column4: and they sat and watched him there.
column5: And sitting down they watched him there;

column4: They set up over his head the accusation against him written, “THIS IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS.”
column5: And set up over his head his accusation written, THIS IS JESUS THE KING OF THE JEWS.

column4: Then there were two robbers crucified with him, one on his right hand and one on the left.
column5: Then were there two thieves crucified with him, one on the right hand, and another on the left.

column4: Those who passed by blasphemed him, wagging their heads,
column5: And they that passed by reviled him, wagging their heads,

column4: and saying, “You who destroy the temple, and build it in three days, save yourself! If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross!”
column5: And saying, Thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days, save thyself. If thou be the Son of God, come down from the cross.

column4: Likewise the chief priests also mocking, with the scribes, the Pharisees, and the elders, said,
column5: Likewise also the chief priests mocking him , with the scribes and elders, said,

column4: “He saved others, but he can’t save himself. If he is the King of Israel, let him come down from the cross now, and we will believe in him.
column5: He saved others; himself he cannot save. If he be the King of Israel, let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him.

column4: He trusts in God. Let God deliver him now, if he wants him; for he said, ‘I am the Son of God.’ ”
column5: He trusted in God; let him deliver him now, if he will have him: for he said, I am the Son of God.

column4: The robbers also who were crucified with him cast on him the same reproach.
column5: The thieves also, which were crucified with him, cast the same in his teeth.

column4: Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land until the ninth hour.
column5: Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land unto the ninth hour.

column5: And about the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?

column4: Some of them who stood there, when they heard it, said, “This man is calling Elijah.”
column5: Some of them that stood there, when they heard that , said, This man calleth for Elias.

column4: Immediately one of them ran, and took a sponge, and filled it with vinegar, and put it on a reed, and gave him a drink.
column5: And straightway one of them ran, and took a spunge, and filled it with vinegar, and put it on a reed, and gave him to drink.

column4: The rest said, “Let him be. Let’s see whether Elijah comes to save him.”
column5: The rest said, Let be, let us see whether Elias will come to save him.

column4: Jesus cried again with a loud voice, and yielded up his spirit.
column5: Jesus, when he had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost.

column4: Behold, the veil of the temple was torn in two from the top to the bottom. The earth quaked and the rocks were split.
column5: And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent;

column5: And the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose,

column5: And came out of the graves after his resurrection, and went into the holy city, and appeared unto many.

column4: Now the centurion, and those who were with him watching Jesus, when they saw the earthquake, and the things that were done, feared exceedingly, saying, “Truly this was the Son of God.”
column5: Now when the centurion, and they that were with him, watching Jesus, saw the earthquake, and those things that were done, they feared greatly, saying, Truly this was the Son of God.

column5: And many women were there beholding afar off, which followed Jesus from Galilee, ministering unto him:

column5: Among which was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of Zebedee’s children.

column4: When evening had come, a rich man from Arimathaea, named Joseph, who himself was also Jesus’ disciple came.
column5: When the even was come, there came a rich man of Arimathæa, named Joseph, who also himself was Jesus’ disciple:

column5: He went to Pilate, and begged the body of Jesus. Then Pilate commanded the body to be delivered.

column4: Joseph took the body, and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth,
column5: And when Joseph had taken the body, he wrapped it in a clean linen cloth,

column4: and laid it in his own new tomb, which he had cut out in the rock, and he rolled a great stone against the door of the tomb, and departed.
column5: And laid it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn out in the rock: and he rolled a great stone to the door of the sepulchre, and departed.

column4: Mary Magdalene was there, and the other Mary, sitting opposite the tomb.
column5: And there was Mary Magdalene, and the other Mary, sitting over against the sepulchre.

column4: Now on the next day, which was the day after the Preparation Day, the chief priests and the Pharisees were gathered together to Pilate,
column5: Now the next day, that followed the day of the preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees came together unto Pilate,

column4: saying, “Sir, we remember what that deceiver said while he was still alive: ‘After three days I will rise again.’
column5: Saying, Sir, we remember that that deceiver said, while he was yet alive, After three days I will rise again.

column4: Command therefore that the tomb be made secure until the third day, lest perhaps his disciples come at night and steal him away, and tell the people, ‘He is risen from the dead;’ and the last deception will be worse than the first.”
column5: Command therefore that the sepulchre be made sure until the third day, lest his disciples come by night, and steal him away, and say unto the people, He is risen from the dead: so the last error shall be worse than the first.

column4: Pilate said to them, “You have a guard. Go, make it as secure as you can.”
column5: Pilate said unto them, Ye have a watch: go your way, make it as sure as ye can.

column4: So they went with the guard and made the tomb secure, sealing the stone.
column5: So they went, and made the sepulchre sure, sealing the stone, and setting a watch.

column4: Now after the Sabbath, as it began to dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.
column5: In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulchre.

column4: Behold, there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord descended from the sky, and came and rolled away the stone from the door, and sat on it.
column5: And, behold, there was a great earthquake: for the angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and came and rolled back the stone from the door, and sat upon it.

column4: His appearance was like lightning, and his clothing white as snow.
column5: His countenance was like lightning, and his raiment white as snow:

column4: For fear of him, the guards shook, and became like dead men.
column5: And for fear of him the keepers did shake, and became as dead men .

column4: The angel answered the women, “Don’t be afraid, for I know that you seek Jesus, who has been crucified.
column5: And the angel answered and said unto the women, Fear not ye: for I know that ye seek Jesus, which was crucified.

column4: He is not here, for he has risen, just like he said. Come, see the place where the Lord was lying.
column5: He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.

column4: Go quickly and tell his disciples, ‘He has risen from the dead, and behold, he goes before you into Galilee; there you will see him.’ Behold, I have told you.”
column5: And go quickly, and tell his disciples that he is risen from the dead; and, behold, he goeth before you into Galilee; there shall ye see him: lo, I have told you.

column5: And they departed quickly from the sepulchre with fear and great joy; and did run to bring his disciples word.

column4: As they went to tell his disciples, behold, Jesus met them, saying, “Rejoice!” They came and took hold of his feet, and worshiped him.
column5: And as they went to tell his disciples, behold, Jesus met them, saying, All hail. And they came and held him by the feet, and worshipped him.

column4: Then Jesus said to them, “Don’t be afraid. Go tell my brothers that they should go into Galilee, and there they will see me.”
column5: Then said Jesus unto them, Be not afraid: go tell my brethren that they go into Galilee, and there shall they see me.

column4: Now while they were going, behold, some of the guards came into the city, and told the chief priests all the things that had happened.
column5: Now when they were going, behold, some of the watch came into the city, and shewed unto the chief priests all the things that were done.

column4: When they were assembled with the elders, and had taken counsel, they gave a large amount of silver to the soldiers,
column5: And when they were assembled with the elders, and had taken counsel, they gave large money unto the soldiers,

column4: saying, “Say that his disciples came by night, and stole him away while we slept.
column5: Saying, Say ye, His disciples came by night, and stole him away while we slept.

column4: If this comes to the governor’s ears, we will persuade him and make you free of worry.”
column5: And if this come to the governor’s ears, we will persuade him, and secure you.

column4: So they took the money and did as they were told. This saying was spread abroad among the Jews, and continues until today.
column5: So they took the money, and did as they were taught: and this saying is commonly reported among the Jews until this day.

column4: But the eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had sent them.
column5: Then the eleven disciples went away into Galilee, into a mountain where Jesus had appointed them.

column4: When they saw him, they bowed down to him, but some doubted.
column5: And when they saw him, they worshipped him: but some doubted.

column4: Jesus came to them and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.
column5: And Jesus came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.

column4: Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
column5: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost:

column4: teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.
column5: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.
